title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the continuation of La Longue Marche, in the 'loop equation' part. The objects are:
- \hat\pi_{0,3} (or \hat\Pi_{0,3}): the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,\infty}, the profinite (0,3) Teichmüller group.
- \mathcal M_{0,3}^{\sim}: a group of automorphisms of this structure (with order-3 rotation \rho, inertia generators \sigma_\infty, l_1, and a map \hat\varphi). It is an extension of \mathcal N_{0,3}^{\sim} = \mathfrak S_3 \times \mathcal N_{0,3}^{!\sim} by \hat\Pi_{0,3}^{+}.
- \mathcal N^{!}: the part acting trivially on the three punctures. M^{!}(0) is a distinguished 'normalized' subgroup that splits the earlier extension (24).

Previous page. Grothendieck parametrized N^{!\sim} \cong M^{!\sim}(0) by elements \xi \in \hat\pi_{0,3} satisfying two conditions:
- the 3-cycle relation \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1;
- a second, 'loop' relation \xi = (\hat\varphi(\xi)\sigma_\infty(\hat\varphi(\xi))^{-1}) l_1^{\nu}.
The element u_\xi is given by u_\xi(\sigma_\infty)=(\xi l_1^{-\nu})\sigma_\infty and u_\xi(\rho)=\xi\rho. This is a Drinfeld/Ihara-style description of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group by a 'cocycle' \xi.

Formula (33). It completes the composition law: u_{\xi'} u_\xi = u_{\xi''} with \xi'' = u_{\xi'}(\xi)\cdot\xi'. This is the usual crossed-homomorphism (twisted) multiplication, analogous to f'' = f' \cdot u_{f'}(f) in \widehat{GT}.

(34)–(35). Grothendieck passes from the '\sim' groups to a subgroup marked '\approx' (presumably cut out by the extra loop condition):
- N^{\approx} := \mathfrak S_3 \times N^{!\approx} \subset N^{\sim}.
- M^{\approx} := the inverse image of N^{\approx} in M^{\sim}.
- This gives an extension 1 \to \hat\Pi^{+}_{0,3} \to M^{\approx} \to N^{\approx} \to 1, containing the earlier extension (24) as the inverse image of N^{!\approx}.

(36). Composing with the projection to N^{!\approx} = Ker(N^{\approx} \to \mathfrak S_3) gives a second extension 1 \to \hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3} \to M^{\approx} \to N^{!\approx} \to 1. Its kernel is the preimage of \mathfrak S_3, an extension of \mathfrak S_3 by \hat\Pi^{+}_{0,3}: the profinite orientation-preserving (0,3) modular group including permutations of the punctures. Extension (24) appears as a sub-extension, i.e. the quotient taken by a smaller kernel.

(37). The subgroup M^{!\approx}(0) splits (24) and maps isomorphically onto N^{!\approx}, so it also splits (36). Hence the canonical semidirect product M^{\approx} \cong M^{!\approx}(0) \ltimes \hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3}.

Purpose. This prepares the next page. There the homomorphism \Phi : M^{!\approx}(0)\cdot\hat\Pi_{0,3} \to M^{!\approx}(0)\cdot\hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3}, u\cdot a \mapsto u\,\hat\varphi(a), is defined. Grothendieck compares it with the \Phi of §41, aiming to check effectively (not just up to conjugacy) that the two agree. This is part of his programme of describing the 'Teichmüller tower' symmetry group (GT-type) via the genus-0, n=3 level and its equations.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One point is left implicit: that M^{!\approx}(0) lies in M^{\approx} and meets \hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3} trivially. This follows from its mapping isomorphically onto N^{!\approx}, which is indicated under the brace in (37).
The page contains crossed-out false starts of (36), but the final version is consistent.

ideas.what: Composition law \xi'' = u_{\xi'}(\xi)\xi' for the cocycle parametrization of the GT-type group
ideas.modern_name: Multiplication law in \widehat{GT} (crossed-homomorphism / twisted product of parameters f)
ideas.where_published: Only in these Montpellier notes; the Esquisse only sketches the Teichmüller tower idea

ideas.what: Restricting the automorphism-group extension to a subgroup cut out by the loop equation; decomposing it with kernel the profinite (0,3) modular group including \mathfrak S_3
ideas.modern_name: Extensions Out/Aut of profinite genus-0 mapping class groups, \widehat{GT} acting on \hat\Gamma_{0,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps; Harbater–Schneps; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; later Horel and Boavida–Horel–Robertson
ideas.where_published: Theme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the details here are unpublished

ideas.what: Canonical semidirect product splitting M^{\approx} \cong M^{!\approx}(0) \ltimes \hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3} via a normalized section
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the automorphism extension via normalized (tangential-basepoint) automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; cf. the normalized form of \widehat{GT} elements (Drinfeld, Ihara)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine group-extension bookkeeping (restriction to a subgroup, change of quotient, splitting by an already-known section) in Grothendieck's private development of a GT-type group. The underlying ideas are well covered by the later \widehat{GT} literature. Nothing on this page is a new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'l'image inverse de M_{0,3}^{\sim} de N^{\approx}' should read 'l'image inverse dans M_{0,3}^{\sim} de N_{0,3}^{\approx} \subset N_{0,3}^{\sim}, donc munie aussi d'une structure d'extension' ('quis[?]' = 'aussi').
'Le sous-groupe M^{!\approx}(0), qui[?] une section' should read 'qui est une section de (24)'.
'contenant (24) comme sous-extension du = quotient par un groupe plus petit' means a sub-extension, i.e. a quotient by a smaller group.
In the crossed-out line, 'souris[?]' is likely 'sous-groupe'.
The heading line shows a crossed-out label before (33).
